records.limits: Projects and agents measure programme throughput, not whether the adopted tools raise productivity, remain in use or narrow the digital divide. The results page is a programme dashboard updated in 2026 and does not provide a counterfactual for firms that did not receive a grant. Projects can be delivered to the same beneficiary in multiple agreements, and agent counts include providers rather than unique firms served.

pattern.mechanism: Red.es standardised eligible solutions and payment rules, while private agents supplied implementation and volunteer representatives handled applications for firms that lacked administrative capacity. The public side made demand legible and portable; the private side supplied local skills and delivery capacity.
preconditions: A public grant and verification platform that can process many small awards
A pre-qualified supplier network with enough geographic reach to serve rural firms
Simple application and justification rules plus intermediaries who can assist digitally excluded owners
pattern.travelled: Voucher programmes travel when the state defines an interoperable menu and pays on verified delivery. Spain's agent network shows the reach gained by outsourcing implementation, while its project count keeps the risk of double-counting visible.

records.title: AVE high-speed rail network
records.claim: Spain expanded high-speed rail from the first Madrid–Seville line in 1992 to more than 4,000 kilometres of high-speed track by 2024; the Transport Ministry reported that the service reached 70 percent of the population.

source.publisher: Government of Spain, Ministry of Transport statement to the 2024 International Transport Forum

records.limits: Track length and population reach show a sustained national build-out, not whether each corridor earns its operating cost, how much construction exceeded initial budgets or whether travel shifted from cars and planes. The ministry's statement uses a rounded lower bound for the network and a population denominator rather than land-area coverage. Lines and services opened over three decades under different governments, so the record is not a single-project causal test.

pattern.mechanism: Spain treated high-speed rail as a long-horizon territorial network, retained a national infrastructure manager and sequenced corridors over multiple administrations. European funding, domestic engineering capacity and a common technical standard let each new line add value to a growing national system.
preconditions: A stable national investment pipeline that survives electoral cycles
An infrastructure manager able to plan track, signalling, stations and maintenance as one network
Demand, finance and environmental appraisal strong enough to choose where extension is justified
pattern.travelled: Spain's network is a reference case for countries weighing high-speed rail, but the transferable capability is continuity of planning and network integration, not the kilometre target alone.

records.title: La Palma volcanic-eruption recovery and monitoring
records.claim: After the Cumbre Vieja eruption began on 19 September 2021, Spain coordinated a state–Canary Islands–island recovery commission; by February 2024 the state reported €929 million mobilised and 650 CO2 monitoring devices installed, allowing more than 220 families to return safely to homes in affected areas.

metric.name: State resources mobilised for La Palma recovery

secondMetric.name: CO2 monitoring devices installed in affected areas

source.publisher: Government of Spain, La Moncloa recovery commission report

records.limits: Mobilised resources and monitoring devices measure administrative response and a specific safety intervention, not the completeness of reconstruction, the speed and fairness of compensation or long-term livelihood recovery. The €929 million is a government total against its valuation of damage and includes different instruments over several years. The return of more than 220 families to monitored homes is an operational output, not proof that every affected zone was safe.

pattern.mechanism: Spain created a mixed commission linking the central government, the autonomous region, island government and municipalities, then paired large-scale aid with a locally targeted monitoring system. The CO2 programme turned a continuing hazard into a measured re-entry protocol rather than treating the end of the eruption as the end of the emergency.
preconditions: Clear authority to coordinate national funds with regional and municipal reconstruction decisions
Scientific monitoring that can translate a changing hazard into household-level safety rules
A recovery budget that remains available after media attention and the acute emergency decline
pattern.travelled: Post-disaster recovery travels through coordination and monitoring more than through a single grant. La Palma shows how a small island can use national fiscal capacity while keeping local authorities in the operational loop.

records.title: Castor underground gas storage, and its closure
records.claim: Spain extinguished the Castor underground gas-storage concession in October 2014 after seismic events halted operation; the state transferred administration to Enagás and the decree recognised €1.350729 billion in compensation for the former concessionaire, with recovery structured over 30 years.

metric.name: Compensation recognised for the extinguished Castor concession

secondMetric.name: Recovery period authorised through the gas-system charge

source.publisher: Boletín Oficial del Estado, Royal Decree-Law 13/2014 and subsequent constitutional review

records.limits: The compensation and recovery period show the fiscal and legal consequences of closing the facility, not the full construction cost, the number of earthquakes caused or the eventual cost of sealing the wells. The concession was extinguished and the facility placed in hibernation, with later court decisions changing parts of the payment mechanism. This is evidence of a project that could not be operated safely, not a claim that every underground storage project has the same risk.

pattern.mechanism: The state granted a private concession for strategic gas storage, then halted injection when induced seismicity made operation unacceptable and transferred administration to the system operator. The exit preserved the physical asset and safety responsibility but socialised a large compensation claim, showing how a rapid stop can still leave a long fiscal tail.
preconditions: Independent seismic monitoring and a regulator able to suspend operation on safety grounds
A concession contract that defines compensation, decommissioning and liability before construction
A system operator capable of securing and maintaining a closed facility while its final fate is decided
pattern.travelled: Castor travels as a caution about subsurface megaprojects and asymmetric risk: stopping unsafe operation is necessary, but the public needs an honest liability and decommissioning plan before approving the investment.

records.title: mObywatel digital ID wallet
records.claim: Poland made the mDowód digital identity document in the mObywatel app legally equivalent to the physical identity card inside Poland; the Ministry of Digital Affairs reports that eight million people use the document, which can also support PESEL blocking and other public-service interactions.

metric.name: People using the mDowód digital identity document

secondMetric.name: Legal status of mDowód inside Poland

source.publisher: Polish Ministry of Digital Affairs, mObywatel usage update

records.limits: The user count measures adoption of a government wallet, not successful completion of public services, equal access for people without compatible phones or the privacy and fraud risks of concentrating documents in one app. The ministry reports a rounded current total and does not state how often each user presents the credential. Legal equivalence applies in Poland and does not automatically make the document a cross-border EU credential.

pattern.mechanism: Poland put a verifiable identity document and several high-value public functions in one mobile wallet, then gave the digital document explicit legal standing so offices, banks and other authorised institutions could accept it. A central app reduced the need for each service to build its own mobile credential.
preconditions: A trusted national population register and physical identity issuance system
A state operator able to sign and revoke verifiable mobile documents
A legal rule that tells frontline institutions when a digital document is equivalent to paper
pattern.travelled: Digital wallets travel when legal recognition follows technical deployment. Poland's adoption shows the pull of a useful document, while the single-app design keeps recovery and exclusion as live governance questions.

records.title: Rodzina 500+ and 800+ child-benefit delivery
records.claim: Poland's ZUS-administered child-benefit system has paid support since 2016 and moved applications and payments online; by November 2023, the government reported nearly seven million children reached and almost PLN255 billion transferred, before the monthly benefit rose from 500 to 800 złoty in January 2024.

metric.name: Children reached by Rodzina 500+ since launch

secondMetric.name: Support transferred through the programme since launch

source.publisher: Polish Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy, Rodzina 800+ announcement

records.limits: The cumulative transfer and child counts show administrative reach, not poverty reduction, fertility effects, take-up among eligible families or the programme's fiscal sustainability. The government reports rounded totals and the period includes a change from 500+ to 800+, so the numbers do not describe one constant benefit. Payments are made to bank accounts, leaving delivery quality dependent on digital access and accurate beneficiary records.

pattern.mechanism: Poland turned a broad entitlement into a single national payment workflow, then shifted administration to ZUS and required online applications through ZUS, Emp@tia or bank channels. Automatic uprating from 500 to 800 złoty preserved continuity for existing families without a new eligibility decision.
preconditions: A population and social-insurance register that can match children to guardians
A payment agency with nationwide bank-transfer and fraud-control capacity
Assisted application routes for households that cannot navigate online forms
pattern.travelled: Large child-benefit systems travel when payment infrastructure is simpler than case-by-case welfare administration. Poland's digital-only application rule shows the efficiency gained and the inclusion risk that must be managed alongside it.

records.title: Baltic Pipe gas interconnection
records.claim: Poland's Gaz-System, Denmark's Energinet and Norway's Gassco coordinated the Baltic Pipe cross-border gas corridor; the interconnection launched on 1 October 2022 and reached its target technical parameters by November, allowing up to 10 billion cubic metres per year toward Poland.

source.publisher: Polish Energy Regulatory Office, National Report of the President of URE 2023

records.limits: Capacity and commissioning dates show infrastructure delivered, not actual annual flows, gas-price effects, environmental costs or the security value of a single corridor under changing demand. The regulator reports technical parameters and the three-operator arrangement, while the project also depended on EU and national permitting outside this metric. The record describes a cross-border build rather than a purely Polish project.

pattern.mechanism: Three transmission-system operators aligned standards, permits, offshore construction and compressor upgrades around one operating date. Poland's public strategy created the demand and political priority, while the network companies supplied the engineering and cross-border interfaces needed to make the corridor usable.
preconditions: Regulators and transmission operators with authority to coordinate across borders
A shared technical and permitting plan for offshore and onshore assets
An anchor demand and financing model strong enough to justify capacity before completion
pattern.travelled: Cross-border infrastructure travels through interoperable operators and a single commissioning plan. Baltic Pipe shows how a strategic objective can be converted into a working corridor when national and commercial incentives line up.

records.title: Alert RCB national emergency SMS channel
records.claim: Poland's Government Security Centre launched Alert RCB as an opt-out-free emergency SMS channel in 2018; in its first year it activated the system 23 times and, working with mobile operators, sent about 200 million warning messages to phones in threatened areas.

metric.name: Warning SMS messages sent in Alert RCB's first year

secondMetric.name: Alert RCB activations in its first year

source.publisher: Government Security Centre of Poland, quarterly analytical bulletin no. 27

records.limits: Messages and activations measure the scale of a warning channel, not delivery time, comprehension, false-alarm rates or whether people changed behaviour. The bulletin notes that large-area alerts could take two to three hours to distribute and that phones outside network coverage might not receive them. Roaming can also produce duplicate messages, so SMS volume is not a unique-person count.

pattern.mechanism: RCB receives hazard information from crisis services and meteorological agencies, defines a threatened geography and legally requires every mobile operator to broadcast the same short warning without prior subscription. The channel is deliberately simple and complements local sirens and emergency services.
preconditions: A central crisis authority able to trigger messages across all mobile operators
A geographic targeting system at least as precise as the powiat
Operator capacity and redundant channels for outages, roaming and people outside coverage
pattern.travelled: Mass SMS warnings travel when the state can use operators as a coordinated last-mile network. Poland's early data also makes the latency and duplication limits explicit rather than hiding them behind a reach percentage.

records.title: Ostrołęka C coal block, and its abandonment
records.claim: Poland began the 1,000-MW Ostrołęka C coal-block project in 2018 without full financing, suspended construction in 2020 and demolished the built elements in 2021; the Supreme Audit Office later found that the unfinished investment consumed more than PLN1.5 billion.

metric.name: Cost of the unfinished Ostrołęka C investment

secondMetric.name: Planned electrical capacity of the abandoned coal block

source.publisher: Najwyższa Izba Kontroli (Supreme Audit Office), Ostrołęka C closure audit

records.limits: The audit's cost figure covers the investment and its close-out as assessed by NIK, not every wider system cost or the value of the later gas-fired replacement. The project was a state-owned-company investment rather than a conventional central-government budget line, and the audit is a retrospective accountability finding. Abandonment can prevent further losses, but it does not recover the sunk expenditure or prove that every original energy-security objective was mistaken.

pattern.mechanism: Poland committed to a large coal unit before its financing, fuel assumptions and climate-policy fit were fully re-tested. When the economics and policy context changed, the state-owned investors suspended the build and converted the site toward gas, but only after construction and contractual obligations had made the exit costly.
preconditions: Independent feasibility and financing checks refreshed when a project is materially delayed
Board and shareholder oversight able to stop a state-owned project before sunk costs compound
A site-reuse and worker-transition plan that preserves options after cancellation
pattern.travelled: Ostrołęka travels as a warning about energy megaproject lock-in: changing course is rational when assumptions fail, but review gates must come before construction and contract settlement, not after.

records.title: BankID federated electronic identity
records.claim: Sweden's bank-issued BankID became a shared identity layer for public and private services: in 2024 it handled 7.6 billion identification or signature transactions for 8.6 million users across 7,500 connected services, with 99.99% availability.

source.publisher: Finansiell ID-Teknik BID AB (BankID), 2024 statistics

records.limits: BankID is a private bank consortium rather than a state identity card, and access requires a Swedish personal identity number, an issuing bank and the ability to use the app without assistance. Transaction volume and availability show a functioning identity rail, not equal access, fraud resistance, or the quality of the public services reached through it.

pattern.mechanism: Major banks formed a common issuer and technical standard, then public authorities and firms adopted the same authentication and signing flow instead of each building a separate credential. That let one already-identified customer base become national digital infrastructure without a single government agency issuing every credential.
preconditions: Banks with near-universal customer relationships and reliable know-your-customer records
A stable personal identity number that public and private services can use as the joining key
Public-sector willingness to accept a privately operated identity at a common assurance level
pattern.travelled: BankID travels as a federated-identity pattern: the reusable move is a shared trust and liability framework, not the mobile app alone, and countries without a similarly concentrated banking or identity base will need a different issuer coalition.

records.title: Swish mobile instant payments
records.claim: Sweden's six-bank-owned Getswish consortium built Swish into a national mobile payment rail: in 2023 it served just over 8.7 million private users and about 335,000 merchant or business users, processing approximately 977 million payments worth SEK 480 billion.

source.publisher: Sveriges Riksbank, The Swedish Financial Market 2024

records.limits: The Riksbank's figures are service totals, not a causal evaluation of the consortium or a measure of consumer welfare. Swish depends on mobile BankID, smartphones and participating banks, so people without those prerequisites can be excluded; high payment volume also says nothing about fraud, outage resilience or market competition.

pattern.mechanism: Competing banks jointly owned a simple brand and API, used BankID for authentication and connected the service to the national settlement infrastructure. The consortium solved the coordination problem of getting rival banks to make one person-to-person rail interoperable before merchants and public services built on it.
preconditions: A small group of banks willing to share ownership and a common customer experience
A trusted digital identity already used by most account holders
Settlement infrastructure and rules that can move funds between member banks in seconds
pattern.travelled: Swish travels as a bank-led interoperability pattern. The institutional move is joint governance across rivals; the app's reach depends on the identity, handset and settlement layers underneath it.

records.title: 1177 national health portal and helpline
records.claim: Sweden's regions and municipalities run the 1177 national health hub through Inera, combining a common website, logged-in care services and the nationwide nurse helpline; 1177.se recorded just over 260 million visits in 2021 and the telephone service answers more than five million calls per year.

source.publisher: Swedish eHealth Agency, Follow-Up Vision for eHealth 2025 (report on 2021)

records.limits: The 2021 web total includes an exceptional pandemic information load, while the call figure is a rounded annual capacity measure from 1177 rather than a contemporaneous count. Regions still run their own advice operations and decide which logged-in services and records are visible, so national branding does not mean identical service quality or outcomes everywhere.

pattern.mechanism: Regional health systems kept operational responsibility but agreed on one national entry point, shared content standards and a common identity-backed service layer. The arrangement turns a fragmented provider landscape into a recognisable front door without removing regional control over care.
preconditions: A durable inter-regional body able to maintain common content, interfaces and support
A national identity and consent model for exposing records and care transactions
Regional funding and governance that can keep local services connected to the shared platform
pattern.travelled: 1177 travels as a federated public-service portal: a common national front door can coexist with decentralised delivery when the shared layer is narrow, maintained and trusted.

records.title: VMA multi-channel public warning system
records.claim: Sweden's Viktigt meddelande till allmänheten (VMA) system combines radio, television, mobile messages, apps and outdoor sirens; SOS Alarm's 2025 report records 37 VMA alerts issued in 2024, alongside the four scheduled annual siren tests.

source.publisher: SOS Alarm, 112 Report 2025

records.limits: Alert count measures the activation of a warning chain, not the share of people who received, understood or acted on a message. Outdoor sirens do not cover every location, mobile delivery depends on network and handset conditions, and scheduled tests are evidence of maintenance rather than proof of performance in a major disaster.

pattern.mechanism: Authorised authorities can request one centrally coordinated warning, while SOS Alarm and broadcasters distribute it through several channels and the siren network is exercised on a fixed public schedule. Redundancy makes the warning less dependent on any one medium and gives residents a familiar routine for checking what a signal means.
preconditions: A legally defined authority and a single operational gateway for issuing warnings
Agreements with broadcasters, mobile operators and municipalities that keep channels interoperable
Regular public tests and clear instructions that convert a signal into protective action
pattern.travelled: VMA travels as a layered-warning pattern: countries can add mobile and app channels without discarding sirens and broadcast, but only if the trigger authority and message vocabulary stay unambiguous.

records.title: Nya Karolinska Solna public–private hospital project
records.claim: Stockholm delivered Nya Karolinska Solna through a 30-year public–private partnership: the official inquiry reports SEK 22.8 billion for construction and equipment, a projected SEK 57 billion total through 2040 including operation and maintenance, and an external comparison that found construction 53% more expensive per square metre than Scandinavian hospitals.

metric.name: Nya Karolinska construction and equipment investment

secondMetric.name: Estimated construction cost premium per square metre

source.publisher: Swedish Government Official Inquiry SOU 2020:15, published by Sveriges riksdag

records.limits: The inquiry distinguishes the 22.8 billion construction-and-equipment investment from the 57 billion projection through 2040, which includes operations, maintenance, financing and additions; those figures are not a like-for-like cash budget. The 53% comparison is an external estimate with explanations including higher standards, site conditions, schedule and PPP risk transfer, so it does not isolate one causal failure or measure clinical performance.

pattern.mechanism: Stockholm bundled design, construction, financing, operations and maintenance into a long PPP contract, transferring construction risk and locking in a lifecycle payment model. The inquiry shows the trade-off: a complex hospital was delivered and remains in use, but the long contract and specification changes made the full cost harder to compare and challenge.
preconditions: A public buyer able to specify a complex clinical programme before contracting
Independent financial, clinical and risk scrutiny that can test a PPP against conventional procurement
Governance that keeps service requirements and change control aligned over a multi-decade contract
pattern.travelled: Nya Karolinska travels as a cautionary PPP pattern: lifecycle contracts can bundle accountability, but benchmarkers need to separate build cost, financing, maintenance and service outcomes before calling a project efficient.

records.title: Barsebäck nuclear plant closure and decommissioning
records.claim: Sweden permanently shut Barsebäck 1 in 1999 and Barsebäck 2 in 2005; the national nuclear-safety report lists each reactor at 615 MWe and records the site as undergoing decommissioning, a 1,230-MWe asset retirement completed by political decision rather than construction failure.

metric.name: Net electrical capacity permanently retired at Barsebäck

source.publisher: Swedish Radiation Safety Authority, Sweden's Tenth National Report under the Convention on Nuclear Safety

records.limits: Retiring a nuclear asset is evidence about a state's ability to close and decommission a major system, not about whether the original plant was safe, economical or replaceable without wider grid effects. Capacity is nameplate output rather than annual generation, and the record does not quantify replacement power, compensation or the final decommissioning cost.

pattern.mechanism: Sweden converted a political decision into a regulated, staged retirement: operators removed fuel, kept the site under care and maintenance, and moved toward dismantling under the nuclear-safety authority's oversight. The capability is visible in the exit path and accountability after closure, not only in the original build.
preconditions: A regulator with authority to supervise shutdown, fuel removal and decommissioning
Long-lived financing and liability arrangements for an asset that no longer produces revenue
A replacement-power and local-transition plan that makes a politically chosen closure workable
pattern.travelled: Barsebäck travels as a durable-exit pattern: a benchmark should count the institutional work of retiring infrastructure, while keeping the energy trade-offs separate from the fact of closure.

records.title: MyGovID single sign-on for public services
records.claim: Ireland built MyGovID as a reusable online identity for welfare, tax, transport, education and childcare services; the 2025 Digital Decade country report records more than 2.7 million verified accounts in December 2024, close to 65% of adults.

secondMetric.name: Verified accounts as share of adults

source.publisher: European Commission, Digital Decade 2025 Ireland country report

records.limits: Verified accounts are a reach measure, not proof that every service is available or easy to use. The account requires identity-verification steps and a Public Services Card or equivalent route, and the adult-share denominator excludes children and people who remain offline; one account can also be used for many services without showing the quality of those transactions.

pattern.mechanism: Ireland joined identity verification run by the Department of Social Protection to a common sign-on adopted by other departments, so each service could reuse one assurance process rather than issue its own credentials. The account layer makes cross-department integration visible to citizens while leaving service ownership distributed.
preconditions: A national identity-verification process that can be reused by multiple departments
A stable personal service number and legal basis for linking benefits and tax services
A central product owner with authority to set authentication and accessibility standards
pattern.travelled: MyGovID travels as a government-wide identity pattern: a single sign-on only joins services when the back-end data, assurance rules and fallback routes are coordinated as carefully as the login screen.

records.title: National Broadband Plan rural fibre rollout
records.claim: Ireland's National Broadband Plan combined commercial investment with a state intervention contract for rural areas covering more than 560,000 premises; by October 2024 the government reported over 102,600 premises connected to the National Broadband Ireland network.

source.publisher: Government of Ireland, National Broadband Plan benefits and rollout update

records.limits: The connection count is a rollout snapshot, not completion of the national plan or a measure of connection quality, take-up, affordability or economic impact. The state-intervention area is a target geography and the programme's future milestones can move with construction, demand and commercial coverage; premises passed and premises connected are different stages.

pattern.mechanism: The state defined a universal-service gap, subsidised a network builder in that gap and left commercially viable areas to private operators. A single contract, a published intervention map and connection points for community facilities let public policy steer private construction without requiring the state to own every fibre asset.
preconditions: A reliable map distinguishing commercial coverage from premises no operator will serve
A procurement and subsidy contract with milestones, open access and clawback protections
An independent regulator able to monitor build quality, wholesale access and consumer take-up
pattern.travelled: The NBP travels as a gap-subsidy model: public money can extend private networks, but the benchmark must separate premises passed, connected and using the service so a rollout headline does not become a coverage claim.

records.title: National COVID-19 vaccination delivery
records.claim: Ireland's HSE vaccination programme built a national booking, supply and reporting operation during COVID-19; by 21 July 2021 its dashboard recorded 5,344,686 administered doses, including 2,854,040 first doses.

source.publisher: Health Service Executive, COVID-19 vaccination programme dashboard

records.limits: The July 2021 dashboard is an interim administrative snapshot and warns that recorded totals lag some GP vaccinations. Dose counts measure throughput, not equitable access, protection, adverse events or the speed of the programme's later phases; the campaign also depended on global supply and changing clinical guidance.

pattern.mechanism: Ireland combined HSE clinics, general practitioners, pharmacies, a central registration process and national data reporting under one prioritisation strategy. The shared dashboard let planners see supply and administration together while local providers supplied the last mile.
preconditions: A health service able to allocate scarce doses through a published national priority order
Cold-chain logistics and a common reporting system linking hospitals, GPs, pharmacies and clinics
Trusted clinical advice that can change eligibility and dosing rules without fragmenting delivery
pattern.travelled: The vaccination pattern travels as a federated emergency operation: a central queue and data standard can coordinate many providers, but the last-mile workforce and supply contracts determine whether the plan becomes injections.

records.title: National Asset Management Agency crisis workout
records.claim: Ireland created NAMA in response to the property and banking crisis, acquired distressed loans and worked them down through asset sales and development; by the end of 2023 it had generated €47.7 billion in cash and transferred more than €4.25 billion to the Exchequer while preparing an orderly wind-down.

metric.name: Cash generated by NAMA since inception

source.publisher: National Asset Management Agency, 2023 year-end review

records.limits: Cash generated and Exchequer transfers are financial outputs, not a counterfactual estimate of how the crisis would have unfolded without NAMA. Asset sales depend on market conditions, the agency's mandate was exceptional and temporary, and the figures do not capture distributional effects, losses borne elsewhere in the banking system or the full public cost of the rescue.

pattern.mechanism: Ireland isolated distressed property loans in a specialist agency with a statutory mandate, state-backed financing and commercial asset-management skills. Separating workout decisions from the surviving banks created a long time horizon for sales and development while making the agency's cash and wind-down obligations reportable.
preconditions: Legislation that gives a crisis agency clear powers to acquire, restructure and dispose of assets
A credible funding and valuation framework that can survive political and market pressure
Transparent reporting and a sunset or wind-down plan so an emergency institution does not become permanent
pattern.travelled: NAMA travels as a crisis-workout pattern: a temporary balance-sheet institution can create room for recovery, but its public return must be read alongside the losses and guarantees that made the intervention possible.

records.title: New Children's Hospital cost escalation
records.claim: Ireland's New Children's Hospital project saw its approved budget rise from €1.73 billion to €2.24 billion by February 2024 after an independent review recorded €450 million of earlier escalation and weaknesses in set-up, planning, execution and governance.

metric.name: Current approved budget for the hospital project and programme

source.publisher: Department of Health, Government of Ireland, New Children's Hospital budget approval

records.limits: The approved budget includes the main hospital, satellite centres, commissioning, information systems and service integration, so it is not a pure construction-cost comparison. The 2019 review attributes escalation to several interacting factors, and the project was still being delivered when the 2024 budget was approved; the record therefore shows an eroded cost and governance promise, not a completed outcome evaluation.

pattern.mechanism: Ireland kept a politically necessary hospital project moving after cost escalation, but the state had to reset the budget and strengthen assurance rather than re-tender. The case makes the value of early challenge visible: once design, contracts and site work are locked, correcting an underestimated scope becomes more expensive than revising the approval.
preconditions: An independent gateway review that tests scope, budget, risk and delivery capability before construction
A sponsor with enough clinical and commercial expertise to challenge designers and contractors
Change-control rules that expose scope growth and schedule slippage to ministers and the public
pattern.travelled: The hospital travels as a megaproject caution: a reset can preserve a needed public asset, but only an early assurance function can prevent a politically protected project from consuming its contingency before the building opens.

records.title: Met Éireann national weather-warning service
records.claim: Ireland's national meteorological service uses a standard Yellow–Orange–Red warning system and briefs the National Emergency Coordination Group so government departments and agencies can coordinate ahead of severe weather; warnings are issued up to 48 hours before anticipated conditions.

metric.name: Forecast lead time for severe-weather warnings

source.publisher: Met Éireann, Irish Meteorological Service, warning-system guidance

records.limits: Lead time and colour levels describe the warning protocol, not forecast accuracy, public comprehension or whether local authorities reduced harm. The system is hazard-specific and weather-dependent, and a warning is only one input into the National Emergency Coordination Group's operational decisions.

pattern.mechanism: Met Éireann translates forecast uncertainty into a small, nationally understood set of action levels, then places the forecast inside a whole-of-government coordination forum. That joins technical information to a standing decision process instead of leaving each department to interpret raw weather data independently.
preconditions: A national meteorological service with authority and credibility to issue one public scale
A cross-government coordination group that can turn warnings into transport, health and local-response actions
Clear thresholds and public guidance that link each colour to a precaution rather than a vague alert
pattern.travelled: The warning pattern travels when a forecast scale is paired with a coordination forum: colour labels alone do not create preparedness unless agencies know who convenes, decides and communicates next.

records.title: Salário mínimo and its permanent revaluation rule
records.claim: Brazil's Congress and president established a permanent annual valorização do salário mínimo in Law 14.663/2023, setting the national floor at R$1,320 from May 2023 and linking later adjustments to INPC inflation plus real GDP growth from two years earlier.

metric.name: National minimum wage set by Law 14.663/2023

source.publisher: Presidency of the Republic, Law No. 14.663/2023

records.limits: A statutory floor is not the same as wages actually paid or compliance with labour law. The formula does not show real purchasing power, employment, informality, regional cost differences, enforcement or causal effects, and later fiscal-cap legislation altered the practical ceiling on increases. This record documents a national rule for routine adjustment rather than an outcome evaluation.

pattern.mechanism: Congress codified an INPC-plus-lagged-GDP rule, while the Executive issues the annual decree that sets the floor. Linking a visible wage rule to regularly published national indicators makes annual change routine and contestable instead of an ad hoc negotiation.
preconditions: Reliable, timely inflation and national-accounts statistics that can anchor the adjustment formula
National labour-law and payroll enforcement that reaches formal employers and protects the statutory floor
Budget coordination because pensions, social benefits and public-sector pay are indexed to the minimum wage
pattern.travelled: Wage indexation travels as a rule-design pattern, not a universal number: countries can combine inflation and growth, but must decide how to protect purchasing power without amplifying fiscal or employment shocks.

records.title: National basic-research funding allocation
records.claim: China's National Bureau of Statistics, Ministry of Science and Technology and Ministry of Finance reported 225.91 billion yuan in basic-research expenditure in 2023, equal to 6.77% of national R&D spending.

metric.name: Basic-research share of national R&D expenditure

source.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China, Ministry of Science and Technology and Ministry of Finance, 2023 science-and-technology expenditure communiqué

records.limits: The share measures spending classification, not research quality, scientific independence, peer-review quality, frontier breakthroughs or the eventual use of results. The communiqué uses national administrative statistics, reports preliminary GDP inputs and excludes Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, so it is not a complete measure of every Chinese research activity.

pattern.mechanism: China's statistical and science ministries separate basic, applied and experimental R&D in a recurring national account, while public funders protect a basic-research tranche alongside mission-oriented programmes. That makes the long-horizon allocation visible in the same frame as industrial development spending.
preconditions: A national R&D classification that distinguishes basic research from applied work and experimental development
Stable public funders and multi-year grants that can sustain uncertain work beyond an annual policy cycle
A statistical system able to collect comparable expenditure returns from firms, universities and government institutes
pattern.travelled: A basic-research share travels only with a classification and funding system behind it: a percentage without stable grant institutions can be re-labelled spending rather than a durable long-horizon capability.

records.title: UAE Pass, the shared digital identity layer
records.claim: The UAE Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority reported that UAE Pass had 6.84 million registered users accessing more than 15,000 digital services from government and private-sector providers in 2023.

secondMetric.name: Digital services available through UAE Pass

source.publisher: UAE Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority, Digital Enablers Report 2023

records.limits: Registered accounts and listed services do not show active use, completion rates, accessibility, privacy experience or whether a transaction became faster for residents. The figures are reported by the authority coordinating the platform, and provider totals combine government, semi-government and private services with different quality and accountability arrangements.

pattern.mechanism: TDRA coordinated federal and emirate-level governments around one identity, signature and document layer, then allowed banks, telecoms and other private providers to connect to it. A shared authentication rail lets separate organisations reuse verified identity instead of each rebuilding onboarding.
preconditions: A trusted identity and signature framework with privacy, security and liability rules
Technical standards and an integration team able to connect heterogeneous public and private service providers
A large enough service portfolio that users and providers have reason to adopt the common identity
pattern.travelled: Digital identity travels as an ecosystem bargain: a single login scales only when public and private providers share standards and users can see a practical service benefit.

records.title: eNaira, a national rollout with an adoption gap
records.claim: By June 2024, the Central Bank of Nigeria reported 28.46 million eNaira customers onboarded but only 197,041 active wallets, showing that the national CBDC rollout had not converted broad registration into sustained use.

source.publisher: Central Bank of Nigeria, Financial Stability Report June 2024

records.limits: The Central Bank's administrative counts distinguish onboarding from activity but do not explain why wallets became inactive, measure transaction quality or compare the CBDC with Nigeria's much larger private payment rails. The report is the regulator's own account, and the active-wallet figure is a snapshot rather than a causal evaluation of the rollout.

pattern.mechanism: The CBN responded to digital-payment change by launching a sovereign wallet and connecting it to banks, payment providers and identity checks. The gap between customers onboarded and wallets active shows the second task of institutional change: converting a national launch into a habit that survives competing channels.
preconditions: A central bank with legal authority to issue and regulate a digital form of national currency
Interoperability with banks, payment-service providers and identity databases rather than a standalone app
A use case such as reliable transfers or public payments that gives households and merchants a reason to return
pattern.travelled: CBDC rollouts travel as an adoption problem: technical issuance can be national on day one, while active use depends on incentives, reliability and integration with the payment ecosystem.

records.title: Productive Safety Net Programme for drought resilience
records.claim: Ethiopia's government-run Productive Safety Net Programme reached about 8 million people, while 6.8 million received short-term employment in public-works activities that support household income and community resilience.

metric.name: People benefiting from the Productive Safety Net Programme

source.publisher: World Bank Group, Ethiopia country programme overview

records.limits: Beneficiary and public-works counts show administrative reach, not whether transfers arrive on time, food security improves, assets survive drought or households graduate from support. The World Bank summary describes a government programme supported by development partners and does not replace an independent impact evaluation or a complete account of conflict-affected regions.

pattern.mechanism: Ethiopia made drought support predictable through a national safety-net platform that combines transfers for labour-poor households with public works and can scale assistance when shocks arrive. The programme links immediate consumption protection to land, water and community assets rather than treating relief as a one-off distribution.
preconditions: A household and geographic targeting system that can identify chronic food insecurity before a crisis peaks
Local administrative and public-works capacity able to deliver cash, food or employment across remote districts
Early-warning and financing arrangements that release additional support when drought or other shocks exceed normal programme capacity
pattern.travelled: Shock-responsive safety nets travel when predictable core transfers and scalable emergency finance share one delivery system; a relief fund without that backbone cannot expand quickly when conditions change.

records.title: Guatecompras, the national procurement marketplace
records.claim: Guatemala's Ministry of Finance reported 152,676 enabled Guatecompras users in April 2023, including 137,950 registered suppliers alongside public buyers, auditors and oversight bodies using the national procurement system.

source.publisher: Government of Guatemala, Ministry of Public Finance, Guatecompras user report

records.limits: Enabled accounts are not the same as completed tenders, competitive prices, delivered works or lower corruption. The ministry's count is an administrative snapshot and does not show how often suppliers bid, whether data are corrected, or whether every public entity follows the system in practice.

pattern.mechanism: Guatemala put public buyers, suppliers, auditors and oversight bodies on a shared procurement record, giving firms a common route into state demand and giving monitors a common transaction identifier. The platform turns a dispersed paper process into a searchable public-private interface.
preconditions: A procurement rule that requires public entities to publish opportunities and awards in one system
Supplier registration and buyer roles that let firms participate while preserving audit access
A public data interface and complaint or correction process that makes transactions inspectable after award
pattern.travelled: Procurement platforms travel when participation and oversight use the same records: a portal that only publishes winning announcements cannot create the supplier competition or audit trail that Guatecompras attempts.

records.title: National 9-1-1 emergency-response system
records.claim: The Dominican Republic expanded its National 9-1-1 Emergency and Security System to 27 provinces by July 2026, covering 94.64% of the population, or more than 9.6 million people.

metric.name: Population covered by the national 9-1-1 system

source.publisher: Presidency of the Dominican Republic, expansion of the National 9-1-1 System

records.limits: Population coverage and provincial integration show reach, not call-answering speed, dispatch accuracy, survival, crime reduction or equitable service quality. The figures come from the presidency's account of the system, and 5.36% of the population remained outside the stated coverage at the reported date.

pattern.mechanism: The Dominican Republic joined police, health, fire and public-works responders behind one emergency number and expanded the dispatch network province by province. A common protocol and radio system let separate agencies act on the same incident instead of asking residents to coordinate them themselves.
preconditions: A national dispatch centre with authority to route incidents across police, health, fire and transport agencies
Interoperable communications, location data and response protocols that work across provinces
A financing and expansion plan that adds ambulances, staff and local coverage as the service footprint grows
pattern.travelled: Emergency systems travel when a single public interface is backed by interoperable responders and a measured expansion path; the phone number alone is not the capability.

records.title: Sistema Nacional de Emergencias 911
records.claim: Honduras's Sistema Nacional de Emergencias 911 coordinated and attended 762,601 of 788,573 emergency tickets in 2024, reporting 96.71% efficacy through five regional coordination centres.

metric.name: Emergency-ticket coordination and attendance efficacy
metric.unit: % of emergency tickets coordinated and attended

source.publisher: Sistema Nacional de Emergencias 911 de Honduras, Memoria Anual 2024

records.limits: The annual report's ticket counts and efficacy percentage show administrative throughput, not response time, dispatch accuracy, survival, crime reduction or equitable service quality. The figures are the emergency system's own operational accounting, and ticket counts can include calls requiring different agencies or multiple actions; the report does not independently audit the denominator or outcomes.

pattern.mechanism: Honduras put emergency intake, dispatch and inter-agency coordination behind one national 911 service, then operated regional coordination centres to route incidents to the relevant responders. A shared ticket and protocol gives separate agencies a common incident record instead of leaving callers to coordinate them.
preconditions: A national authority able to route incidents across police, health, fire and other response agencies
Interoperable communications, location data and protocols that work between regional centres
Operating budgets and performance reporting that keep centres staffed and reveal where tickets are lost or delayed
pattern.travelled: Emergency coordination travels when a common intake record is backed by interoperable responders and transparent throughput measures; the number alone cannot substitute for the dispatch network behind it.

records.title: Rural electrification and near-universal grid coverage
records.claim: Nicaragua's Ministry of Energy and Mines reported national electricity coverage of 99.575% in December 2024 after public electrification projects brought power to 732,427 homes and 3,853,005 people.

secondMetric.name: Homes electrified through the reported programme

source.publisher: Nicaragua Ministry of Energy and Mines, Electricity Coverage 2024

records.limits: The ministry's coverage and home counts show connection reach, not continuity, affordability, voltage quality, reliability, losses, maintenance or regional inequality. They are government administrative estimates, and the long-run change from the 2006 baseline does not isolate which projects, utilities or financing streams produced the increase.

pattern.mechanism: Nicaragua combined public transmission and distribution investment with rural electrification projects, tracking household coverage as a national delivery target. Extending the grid into remote departments and reporting the remaining gap made a dispersed infrastructure task legible as one programme.
preconditions: A utility and ministry able to plan transmission, distribution and last-mile connections across departments
Capital budgets and procurement arrangements that can reach remote and low-density settlements
A household-level coverage register and maintenance capacity so new connections remain usable after construction
pattern.travelled: Near-universal connection targets travel only with last-mile finance and a maintenance system; a high connection percentage without reliable service can overstate the capability delivered.

records.title: Gran Misión Vivienda Venezuela's five-million-home milestone
records.claim: Venezuela's Gran Misión Vivienda Venezuela reported delivery of its five-millionth home on 7 June 2024, with the programme saying that community self-construction supplied 75% of its construction in the preceding four years.

metric.name: Homes delivered by Gran Misión Vivienda Venezuela

secondMetric.name: Reported share of construction through self-construction

source.publisher: Radio Nacional de Venezuela, report on the GMVV five-million-home milestone

records.limits: The cumulative total is reported by Venezuela's state broadcaster and does not establish independent verification, construction quality, occupancy, maintenance, location, tenure security, cost or whether every unit was newly built rather than rehabilitated. The 75% self-construction figure is a programme claim, and the source supplies no audited project-level cost or schedule data.

pattern.mechanism: Venezuela used a central housing mission to aggregate land, materials and public construction while shifting more of the build into community self-construction. A national target and local delivery groups linked a large capital programme to household-level participation.
preconditions: A central land, finance and materials pipeline that can allocate housing projects across regions
Local organisations able to manage community construction and verify beneficiaries
A housing registry and inspection process that can track units from allocation through occupancy and maintenance
pattern.travelled: Community self-build can extend a state housing programme when it is backed by material supply, technical supervision and a beneficiary registry; without those controls, a headline unit count can conceal unfinished or unoccupied stock.

records.title: National COVID-19 vaccination campaign
records.claim: Cuba's national COVID-19 vaccination campaign had given at least one vaccine dose to 94% of the country's population by 31 December 2021, according to the Pan American Health Organization.

metric.name: Population receiving at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose

source.publisher: Pan American Health Organization, Health in the Americas country profile: Cuba

records.limits: The PAHO coverage figure shows reach of at least one dose, not completion of a primary series, booster uptake, protection against infection, mortality avoided, equity across provinces or the campaign's logistical cost. It is based on reported national data, and the profile does not independently audit Cuba's dose records or distinguish domestically produced vaccines from other supplies.

pattern.mechanism: Cuba treated COVID vaccination as a national public-health delivery operation, using its existing primary-care and community health network to move doses from central procurement and production into local clinics. The campaign's reach depended on routine registration and trusted local health workers rather than a stand-alone emergency site.
preconditions: A nationwide primary-care network with local staff and population registers
Domestic or secured vaccine supply plus cold-chain and scheduling capacity
Public-health surveillance and communication that can identify priority groups and monitor uptake
pattern.travelled: High-coverage emergency vaccination travels when routine primary care, a population register and a dependable supply chain already exist; a campaign launch without those delivery rails cannot reach most households quickly.

records.title: Bitcoin Law, and its 2025 rollback
records.claim: El Salvador's 2025 reform made private-sector Bitcoin acceptance voluntary, limited the law to private participation and repealed Articles 4, 8 and 9 of the 2021 Bitcoin Law.

metric.name: Bitcoin Law articles repealed by the 2025 reform

secondMetric.name: Sectors with mandatory Bitcoin acceptance under the original law

source.publisher: Legislative Assembly of El Salvador, Reforms to the Bitcoin Law (Decree 57/2025)

records.limits: The amendment records a legal rollback, not actual Chivo use, fiscal cost, user adoption, merchant behaviour or whether voluntary acceptance changed after the reform. The comparison with the original law describes the statutory sectors affected; it does not measure how widely the 2021 mandate was followed. The legislative text also cannot by itself establish implementation timing or operational outcomes.

pattern.mechanism: El Salvador launched a national Bitcoin mandate and later used legislation to narrow it: the 2025 reform removed mandatory acceptance, repealed three core articles and confined the legal framework to voluntary private participation. The case makes institutional responsiveness visible as the ability to unwind a national experiment when its obligations no longer fit.
preconditions: A legislature able to amend the legal basis of a national digital-payment programme
Operational monitoring and fiscal or financing feedback that can expose a gap between launch and sustained use
A transition plan that removes public obligations while leaving private actors a voluntary route to continue
pattern.travelled: Policy reversals travel when governments design an exit path before a national experiment becomes permanent infrastructure; without legal clarity, a rollback can leave users, merchants and public agencies with stranded obligations.

records.title: Routine immunization coverage, and its erosion
records.claim: WHO and UNICEF estimated Haiti's national DTP3 routine-immunization coverage at 51% in 2022, down from 68% in 2011, while documenting vaccine and syringe stockouts and weak administrative reporting in the national programme.

metric.name: Estimated DTP3 coverage
metric.unit: % of children receiving three DTP doses

secondMetric.name: Estimated DTP3 coverage at the start of the comparison
secondMetric.unit: % of children receiving three DTP doses

source.publisher: World Health Organization and UNICEF, Estimates of National Immunization Coverage: Haiti 2022 revision

records.limits: The 51% figure is a WHO/UNICEF estimate with low confidence and is not a direct census of vaccinated children: the profile records poor administrative reporting, national stockouts and disagreement from Haiti's Ministry of Health. The estimate does not show which districts lost coverage, whether children completed doses later, or the causal contribution of insecurity, financing, supply or clinic access; it is evidence of a reported national delivery failure, not a clean impact estimate.

pattern.mechanism: Haiti's Expanded Programme on Immunization lost routine coverage as stockouts, insecurity and weak reporting interrupted the chain from national procurement to local clinics. The decline shows how a public-health capability can erode when replenishment, supervision and data feedback fail together, even while the programme remains formally in place.
preconditions: Reliable vaccine and syringe procurement with buffer stocks that can reach every department
A functioning cold chain and clinic network able to offer repeated doses rather than one campaign visit
Accurate child registers and district reporting that expose missed cohorts quickly enough for outreach and corrective supply
pattern.travelled: Immunization systems can recover through catch-up campaigns and community outreach, but the Haiti case warns that a formal national programme is not durable without stock management, trusted local access and data that decision-makers believe.

records.title: Korean regulatory-sandbox system across eight sectors
records.claim: South Korea expanded its regulatory-sandbox system from ICT and industrial-convergence fields in January 2019 to eight sectoral regimes by 2024, adding finance, regulatory-free zones, smart cities, R&D zones, mobility and circular economy testing.

source.publisher: Government of the Republic of Korea, Regulatory Sandbox portal

records.limits: The regime count shows institutional breadth, not the number of firms approved, experiments completed, commercial products launched, safety outcomes or permanent rule changes. The government portal describes the system's design and expansion but does not independently evaluate whether each sectoral track is active at the same intensity or produces net social benefit.

pattern.mechanism: South Korea created a common regulatory-sandbox architecture with temporary permits, demonstration exemptions and rapid regulatory confirmation, then added sector-specific tracks and dedicated support bodies so smaller firms could test products without negotiating every rule from scratch.
preconditions: A legal framework that allows time-, place- and scale-limited exemptions while retaining safety controls
Specialist ministries and intake bodies able to assess experiments across finance, mobility, ICT and industrial sectors
A route from a successful test to regulatory revision, licensing or procurement rather than leaving pilots stranded
pattern.travelled: Sandbox systems travel when experimentation, safeguards and rule-change pathways are designed together; multiplying sector labels without review capacity creates a catalogue rather than a learning system.

records.title: MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox variants
records.claim: Singapore's Monetary Authority operates three FinTech Regulatory Sandbox variants—Sandbox, Sandbox Express and Sandbox Plus—giving firms distinct routes to test regulated products with real customers under defined safeguards.

source.publisher: Singapore Economic Development Board, overview of the MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox

records.limits: Counting three sandbox routes shows regulatory design and breadth, not applications received, firms graduating to full licences, customer protection, failure rates or the cost of supervision. The EDB account is an official ecosystem description and includes illustrative company cases rather than an independent evaluation of all experiments.

pattern.mechanism: MAS made experimentation a staged regulatory service: firms needing tailored controls use the original sandbox, lower-risk activities can use Sandbox Express, and promising proposals can receive a streamlined route with support. Each variant keeps a live test bounded while giving the regulator evidence before a full licence.
preconditions: A financial regulator with authority to vary requirements temporarily and monitor live customer activity
Clear entry, boundary and exit criteria so a sandbox does not become indefinite unlicensed operation
A dense financial and technology ecosystem in which tested products can find counterparties, capital and a path to licensing
pattern.travelled: Regulatory sandboxes travel best as a portfolio matched to risk: one universal process can be too slow for low-risk tests and too loose for products that move real money.

records.title: Knowledge Transfer Partnerships
records.claim: UKRI reported more than 1,000 Knowledge Transfer Partnerships running at one time and more than 1,100 Associate projects in May 2026, joining businesses with universities or other research organisations through jointly supervised innovation work.

source.publisher: UK Research and Innovation, Knowledge Transfer Partnerships overview

records.limits: The partnership and project counts show programme scale, not whether collaborations produce durable productivity, patents, spinouts or jobs. UKRI reports the programme's administrative totals and benefit estimates; participation is not a representative sample of all UK firms or universities, and the figures do not provide a counterfactual against which the programme's effects can be judged.

pattern.mechanism: Innovate UK funds a three-way arrangement in which a business names a strategic problem, a university or research organisation supplies expertise and a graduate associate works inside the firm under joint supervision. The structure gives firms absorptive capacity while giving academic knowledge a route into operations.
preconditions: Research organisations with staff who can translate academic methods into business projects
Firms willing to co-fund a 12–36 month project and give the associate a real strategic problem
A national intermediary that matches partners, sets quality rules and carries lessons between projects
pattern.travelled: Knowledge-transfer partnerships travel when the intermediary funds the bridge and the firm owns a concrete problem; generic networking events rarely create the same embedded learning or accountability.

records.title: Compte personnel de formation
records.claim: France's Compte personnel de formation generated 1,387,500 training starts in 2024, with 1,232,100 people entering a CPF-funded course through the national account and platform.

source.publisher: French Ministry of Labour, DARES Results: Le compte personnel de formation en 2024

records.limits: Training starts and participant counts show use of a public financing and matching platform, not course completion, learning quality, job mobility, wage gains or equal access. DARES notes major catalogue and contribution-rule changes during 2024, including the motorcycle-licence expansion and a €100 co-payment, so year-on-year totals are not a pure measure of underlying learning demand.

pattern.mechanism: France gave individuals a portable training entitlement, then put the account, catalogue, identity checks and payment flow into one national platform managed by the Caisse des Dépôts. The design lets workers choose a course while public employment services and employers can add targeted funding.
preconditions: A national entitlement and contribution system that records rights across employers and employment spells
A trusted digital identity, provider catalogue and payment system that can verify courses and prevent fraud
Quality assurance and co-funding rules that keep a large open marketplace from becoming a directory of low-value training
pattern.travelled: Individual learning accounts travel when entitlement portability is paired with provider quality controls and guidance; a wallet without trusted course information can increase transactions without increasing skills.

records.title: Volunteer fire corps, and its membership erosion
records.claim: Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency reported 732,223 volunteer fire-corps members on 1 April 2025, a fall of 14,458 in one year in the local disaster-response corps that it describes as a core of community resilience.

source.publisher: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency, 2025 White Paper on Fire Service

records.limits: Membership is a capacity proxy, not the number of volunteers who turn out, hours trained, response quality or lives and property protected. The agency reports a one-year decline but this record does not identify its causes or establish a long-run causal trend; local corps differ in duties, age structure and recruitment, and the national total can hide uneven resilience.

pattern.mechanism: Japan embeds trained local volunteers in municipal fire organisations, gives them equipment and a formal role in prevention and disaster response, and is now adding function-specific and student units as the general membership base shrinks. The erosion shows that a long-standing civic institution needs an active recruitment and role-design strategy to remain deployable.
preconditions: Municipal fire organisations able to train, equip and insure residents who serve alongside professional crews
A social norm and compensation structure that make recurring emergency service compatible with work and family life
Flexible roles, youth and women recruitment, and a data system that reveals membership and participation gaps
pattern.travelled: Volunteer emergency corps travel when local legitimacy is matched with practical support and flexible participation; simply asking communities to volunteer does not replace equipment, training or a reason to stay.

records.title: British Patient Capital, a public venture-capital catalyst
records.claim: The British Business Bank reported that government-owned British Patient Capital had committed £2.287 billion through 80 fund commitments, 10 co-investments and 18 Future Fund deals by 31 March 2024, with an underlying portfolio of 1,350 companies.

metric.name: British Patient Capital commitments since inception

source.publisher: British Business Bank, British Patient Capital 2023–24 full-year results

records.limits: Commitments, assets and portfolio-company counts are administrative programme totals, not venture capital as a share of GDP, additionality, exits, jobs or causal economic impact. The portfolio includes third-party fund capital and co-investments, and the figures are reported by the government-owned delivery institution rather than independently evaluating what would have happened without it.

pattern.mechanism: The UK used a public, long-horizon investment platform to anchor private funds, make selected co-investments and keep capital flowing into innovative companies that can be underserved by shorter-horizon finance. A fund-manager network spreads sourcing and specialist judgement beyond the state balance sheet.
preconditions: A public investment institution with a mandate, capital and governance that can tolerate long time horizons
Private fund managers and co-investors able to select, price and support high-growth firms
A pipeline of investable companies and follow-on capital so an anchor commitment can compound rather than stand alone
pattern.travelled: Public venture catalysts travel when they crowd in capable private managers and preserve commercial decision-making; a state fund without deal flow, follow-on finance or disciplined governance can become a subsidy ledger rather than a capital market.

records.title: ICURe, from university research to spinouts
records.claim: UK Research and Innovation's ICURe impact report says spinout companies from the programme secured £326 million in investment funding and created more than 1,400 jobs from 2014 onward, after research teams were trained and funded to test markets before deciding whether to spin out.

source.publisher: UK Research and Innovation, ICURe impact report

records.limits: The impact report's cumulative investment and job figures cover teams supported by ICURe and do not show the full spinout population, survival, profitability, quality of jobs, counterfactual or the programme's independent contribution. They are programme impact estimates, not a national spinout rate or a guarantee that every participating discovery should become a company.

pattern.mechanism: ICURe gives research teams funding, coaching and a disciplined market-discovery period in which they conduct more than 100 customer interviews before a university-backed go/no-go decision. Teams advised to spin out can then apply for follow-on funding, turning technology-transfer work into an investable proposition rather than treating a patent as a company.
preconditions: Universities and research institutes with discoveries, translational staff and authority to support commercial routes
Researchers willing to test a problem with users and founders able to lead a company after the discovery phase
Follow-on grants, investors and technology-transfer offices that can carry a validated opportunity beyond the programme
pattern.travelled: Spinout pipelines travel when market discovery, founder formation and follow-on capital are designed as one chain; a grant or patent alone does not create the commercial capabilities and decisions needed for a durable firm.

records.title: Ramp Up, PROCOMER's export-readiness programme
records.claim: Costa Rica's export agency PROCOMER reported that 40 SMEs graduated from its 16-week Ramp Up 2024 programme, delivered with INA and the Sistema de Banca para el Desarrollo, bringing the number of firms benefiting since the programme began in 2021 to 175.

source.publisher: PROCOMER, Ramp Up 2024 export-capability programme

records.limits: Graduation and reach counts show programme delivery, not verified export growth, new markets, product diversification, export survival or causal impact. PROCOMER describes the firms as strengthening export capability; the source does not establish that all graduates exported or that the programme changed Costa Rica's aggregate concentration.

pattern.mechanism: PROCOMER, the national training institute and a development bank combine practical training in finance, strategy, governance and sustainability with export-market connections. The package builds the organisational routines and compliance readiness that small firms need before an overseas buyer or distributor can become repeat business.
preconditions: An export agency that can identify firms, broker market access and coordinate services rather than offering disconnected workshops
SMEs with a product, management time and enough operational capacity to act on finance, quality and sustainability work
Training, development finance and buyer or standards networks that remain available after graduation
pattern.travelled: Export-readiness programmes travel when capability-building is tied to real market links and finance; a course certificate without buyer validation, working capital or standards support rarely diversifies exports by itself.

records.title: Cooperative Research Centres programme
records.claim: Australia's Department of Industry reported that its Cooperative Research Centres portfolio facilitated 304 businesses establishing research-focused collaborations in 2023–24, across 114 CRC and 190 CRC Projects partners, above the year's target of 248.

source.publisher: Australian Department of Industry, Science and Resources, Annual Report 2023–24

records.limits: The partner count measures collaborations facilitated through grant agreements, not completed research, commercialisation, additionality or university-only links. It is an administrative portfolio measure whose reporting and retrospective calculations can change, and partners include research organisations and community bodies alongside universities and businesses.

pattern.mechanism: Australia funds industry-led research centres for three to ten years and shorter CRC Projects for up to three years, giving firms and researchers a shared programme, matching resources and a governance structure for applied work. The long and short formats let a mature collaboration and a focused translation project coexist.
preconditions: Universities, research organisations and firms able to define a problem together and commit staff or cash
A competitive public grant process with independent assessment and enough duration for trust and technical work to accumulate
A centre-level governance and intellectual-property framework that can turn joint research into adoption or further investment
pattern.travelled: University–industry centres travel when public grants buy durable shared capacity and firms own a consequential problem; short networking schemes without governance, matching effort or a path to adoption produce thinner ties.

records.title: Business-funded R&D as the UK's dominant research sector
records.claim: The Office for National Statistics reported that UK businesses performed £50.0 billion of R&D in 2023, 69% of the country's £72.6 billion gross domestic R&D total.

source.publisher: UK Office for National Statistics, Gross domestic expenditure on research and development: UK 2023

records.limits: The 69% share is a national R&D composition measure, not evidence that business research is basic, additional, productive or evenly distributed across firms and regions. ONS changed the business-survey methods for 2022, so the long historical series needs care; the figures measure R&D performed in UK organisations regardless of the ultimate owner's country.

pattern.mechanism: The UK combines a large private R&D base with public research funding and tax support, leaving firms as the main performers of national R&D while universities and government supply complementary research and talent. The sector mix gives commercial problems a route into the research system, but it also makes the national portfolio sensitive to corporate concentration and cycles.
preconditions: Firms with the cash flow, engineering talent and appropriable returns needed to sustain R&D beyond a single grant
Universities and public laboratories that train researchers and can collaborate with or supply firms
Stable measurement, intellectual-property rules and public co-funding that make long-horizon private research investable
pattern.travelled: A business-led R&D mix travels when private firms have reasons to keep investing and public institutions fill the basic-research and talent gaps; a high share alone can also reflect a few concentrated corporate laboratories.

records.title: Singapore's national ICT-skills measurement and baseline
records.claim: Singapore's Department of Statistics ICT-skills table reports 99.0% in the total row for residents aged 16–74 in 2025, while 55.2% could use a basic arithmetic formula in a spreadsheet; the government uses the series to track SDG 4.4.1 and its Digital Skills for Life framework.

metric.name: Residents with an ICT skill in the total row

source.publisher: Singapore Department of Statistics, annual ICT-skills dataset (IMDA source)

records.limits: The table records task-specific self-reported or survey-derived skills for Singapore residents, not independently tested proficiency, workplace transfer or equal access. The age base changed from residents aged 15 and above in 2016–2020 to ages 16–74 from 2021, and a high total can hide weak performance on harder tasks such as spreadsheet work.

pattern.mechanism: Singapore pairs a recurring skills measurement with a public baseline framework, Digital Skills for Life, and targeted support such as Seniors Go Digital. The combination makes digital capability a population service obligation rather than a one-off computer course, while the task rows reveal where basic access still masks deeper gaps.
preconditions: A statistical agency and digital ministry able to repeat a common task taxonomy and publish the results
Universal connectivity and trusted public services that give adults reasons to practise digital tasks in daily life
Accessible coaching, devices and safety guidance for older and lower-income residents who are least likely to learn informally
pattern.travelled: Digital-skills programmes travel when measurement, everyday use and targeted help reinforce one another; connectivity statistics alone can conceal a population that still cannot complete consequential tasks.

records.title: Singapore Courts' case-clearance discipline
records.claim: Singapore's State Courts disposed of 21,816 civil cases against 20,358 filings in 2023, a 107% civil clearance rate; its Community Justice and Tribunals courts recorded a 99% clearance rate in the same year.

secondMetric.name: Community Justice and Tribunals clearance rate

source.publisher: Singapore Judiciary, Caseload statistics 2023

records.limits: Clearance is disposals divided by filings in the same year, so it can exceed 100% when courts work through earlier stock; it does not show timeliness, fairness, legal-aid access, enforcement or the quality of decisions. The Singapore figures cover court workloads and are not a comparable cross-country civil-justice index without harmonised case definitions.

pattern.mechanism: Singapore Courts publish workload by court and case type, set clearance as a management measure and combine procedural reform with specialised tribunals and dispute-resolution pathways.
